evidence.note: New table/scenario-driven test file for the FSM machine package; read the whole part 1/2 chunk (file lines 1-1258) against the task-done rubric.
Checked for TODO/FIXME markers, t.Skip, and eval-style unsafe execution across the shard: none present.
Verified error/failure paths are asserted by code (errs.Is on ERR_* codes) rather than string matching, and that gate/converge/overflow event sequences are asserted explicitly.
Confirmed the shard is a test-only addition with no production source change, so the rubric's missing-tests and duplicate-service-path rules do not apply.

findings.note: Weakened assertion: the warnings check joins two negated predicates with && , so the test only fails when the warning matches neither the WORKFLOW_WARNING prefix nor the loop_without_clean_exit substring. A warning with the right prefix but the wrong atom passes silently; || was almost certainly intended.

Test-isolation hazard: the package-level MaxDiffBytes is set to 2 and restored three lines later by plain assignment rather than defer. If the intervening t.Fatalf fires, MaxDiffBytes stays at 2 for every subsequent test in the package, turning one failure into a cascade of confusing truncation failures. Same pattern for sess.unlock() after sess.advance(), which is not deferred.
